title: Magical Compass — directional attributions
about: Every entry carries its own source and a confidence (high / medium / low). Azimuth is degrees clockwise from true north; -1 means the direction is computed (a bearing to Boleskine) or there is no fixed quarter (the wandering princes). 'goetia' is the app's cross-reference to the Goetia tool, set only where the entry names that same numbered spirit. 'set' is the compass set it is drawn with (the content table compass_sets: one of its layer's chips, or a set of kings); 'adoration', on the Liber Resh entries, names the adoration it is.

caveats: Star Ruby: the 1913 wording is now confirmed from an OCR of the 1913 Wieland first edition (archive.org) and the O.T.O./Celephaïs e-text: roar ΧΑΟΣ (E), scream ΒΑΒΑΛΟΝ (N), say ΕΡΩΣ (W), bellow ΨΥΧΗ (S), going widdershins. The earlier doubt about 'say' vs 'whisper' is resolved. Thelemapedia's version is wrong and should not be used. The revision first appeared in Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), Appendix VI, not 1944: roar ΘΗΡΙΟΝ, say NUIT, whisper BABALON, bellow HADIT. The Celephaïs collation prints the last three in Roman capitals, not Greek.

Star Ruby guardians: the compass points are inferred. The text places the four powers relative to the body (before, behind, right, left) after the operator returns to the centre. They become E, W, S, N only if the operator faces East at that point.

Liber Samekh (new entries): Crowley's Point II notes explicitly put Air in the East, Fire in the South, Water in the West and Earth in the North, with the Adept circling astrally widdershins and making the sign of the Enterer each time he passes the 'Kiblah', the direction of Boleskine. Spirit (Section F) is invoked from the centre facing Boleskine. Confirmed on the magicianandexorcist.org mirror and by search snippets from hermetic.com and sacred-texts. MTP is a 1929 publication, so the notes here are paraphrase only; the barbarous names come from the ancient Greek magical papyrus.

Liber Reguli: the text names compass quarters (N, S, E, W in that order, turning to the left), but the whole rite is aimed at Boleskine. Rodney Orpheus's commentary reads this as making Boleskine the temple's 'East', as in Liber XV. The app could offer 'true quarters' and 'Boleskine = East' modes. The West pentagram names no zodiac sign ('whereby Water is invoked'), so 'Scorpio' was removed.

Boleskine coordinates: OS NGR NH 50847 22116 (Buildings at Risk Register) converts to WGS84 57.2653, -4.4748 (computed with OSGB36→WGS84 Helmert). Wikipedia gives 57.2653°N 4.4747°W, about 6 m apart. The footnote printed with Liber Reguli reads 'Latitude 57.14 N. Longitude 4.28 W.' That is probably degrees and minutes (57°14′N 4°28′W, about 3.6 km off); read as decimal degrees it is about 14 km off, so do not use it. Use the great-circle initial bearing. Wikipedia describes the house as halfway between Foyers and Inverfarigaig; it burned in 2015 and 2019 and reopened after restoration in April 2026.

Elemental quarters vary by system. GD, 777, LBRP, the grade rituals and Liber Samekh: Air E, Fire S, Water W, Earth N. Agrippa's Scale of Four (Bk II ch. 7, checked at esotericarchives): Fire E, Air W, Water N, Earth S, with Michael E, Raphael W, Gabriel N, Uriel S. Liber O Lesser Hexagram: Fire E, Earth S, Air W, Water N. Liber Reguli: Earth E, Fire S, Water W, Air N. A 'Fire East / Air South' swap of the LBRP scheme appears in no GD or Crowley primary text checked; the nearest real sources for Fire in the East are Agrippa and the Hexagram ritual.

Rulers and Kerubim: Agrippa pairs Cherub with Air, Ariel with Earth, the Eagle with Air and the Man with Water. Liber 777 col. LX and the GD reverse the rulers (Ariel = Air, Kerub = Earth). 777 col. XXXVIII lists both 'Eagle, Man' against Air, while the GD grade rituals use the Man's head for Air and the Eagle for Water.

Winds: the directions are confirmed in Agrippa Bk I ch. 6 (Notus S, Boreas N, Zephyrus W, Eurus E, 'called Apeliotes'). Some classical authors make Eurus the south-east wind. No GD paper pairs the winds with elements, so no element is attached to them.

Flashing colours: Air yellow/violet, Fire red/green and Water blue/orange are consistent. Earth is uncertain: Wikipedia, citing Regardie p. 479, gives black with green letters; others give black/white or the four Malkuth colours (777 col. XV: citrine, russet, olive and black). Only secondary citations were checked, hence medium/low.

Enochian: spellings vary between Dee, the GD papers and Crowley. The grade rituals as transcribed give Edelperna, Ra-agiosel, Ic Zod Heh Chal, EMPEH ARSEL GAIOL and EMOR DIAL HECTEGA. According to Wikipedia, Dee's own writings do not attribute the angels to the quadrants in this way; the element-to-quarter mapping of the four tablets (Air E, Fire S, Water W, Earth N) is the Golden Dawn's. EXARP, BITOM, HCOMA and NANTA are the tablets' lines on the Tablet of Union, used as Spirit names.

Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram: the names (YHVH Air, Elohim Fire, El Water, Adonai Earth; Eheieh for active Spirit, AGLA for passive) were checked only through secondary web copies. The 'Supreme' form as usually printed is thought to have been arranged by Regardie from Inner Order material, so it stays medium. Do not confuse it with the LBRP, which uses YHVH E, Adonai S, Eheieh W and AGLA N whatever the element.

Grade divine names: the Earth opening adores 'Adonai ha-Aretz, Adonai Melekh' but invokes with 'Adonai Melekh', so the entry now carries both. The Fire opening says 'Tetragrammaton Tzabaoth', i.e. YHVH Tzabaoth. Checked on the stichtingargus.nl grade-ritual transcriptions.

Sphinx powers: the app's 777.json col. L lists only Noscere (Air), Audere (Water) and Velle (Fire). Tacere for Earth is the standard fourth power but is not in the app's data, so the Earth entry's extra says so.
Neophyte: the candidate is led to the North, 'the place of greatest symbolic darkness', after the obligation, not at first entry; the Stolistes note was corrected.

Liber 777 col. CX (Sepher Yetzirah) is Crowley's mapping (Chesed Height, Geburah Depth, Tiphareth E, Netzach W, Hod S, Yesod N). Other Kabbalistic mappings of the six directions differ (e.g. Chesed South, Geburah North), so it stays medium.

Liber Resh assumes the Northern Hemisphere (face South at noon, North at midnight). Southern-Hemisphere practitioners often face the Sun (North at noon), so offer this as an option. Sunrise and sunset azimuths also swing far from due E/W with the seasons. The app's data/resh.json spells the god 'Khepra'; Liber Resh has 'Khephra'.

Checked against the 1904 printing itself (scan on Wikimedia Commons, File:The Book of the Goetia (Mathers-Crowley, 1904).djvu), not only the 2003 Celephaïs re-set. Observations (four kings) = p. 31, The Invocation of the King and its footnote = p. 43, Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge = p. 59. The 1904 print reads 'AMAYMON, CORSON, ZIMIMAY or ZIMINIAR, and GÖAP'. GÖAP has the umlaut; only the re-set prints GOAP. Page numbers for spirits 1-36 are omitted because the re-set's pagination differs from the 1904 print by about one page.

The footnote to Amaimon in Crowley's Enochian 'Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge' (p. 59) reads 'Or Gaap, Paimon, Zodimay, as the case may be', and the line itself gives 'East, (South, West, North)'. Read in order, that is Amaimon East, Gaap South, Paimon West, Zodimay North. So the Goetia 1904 does contain a Gaap = South attribution, an order-matched reading of Crowley's footnote, which uses 'Gaap' where the Observations have GÖAP. Göap = South has two supports inside the 1904 edition, while Weyer puts Goap in the West. Corson = West rests only on list order, since p. 59 substitutes Paimon for the West. Spirit 33 Gäap is low confidence: his own entry makes Amaymon his King (East), but the footnote treats Gaap as the southern king.

Agrippa's Hebrew names: matched by the order of III.24 (kings E, S, W, N) they would give Samuel E, Azazel S, Azael W, Mahazuel N. Agrippa's own 'Scale of the number four' (II.7) puts Samael, Azazel, Azael and Mahazael in explicit columns with 'The East, The West, The North, The South' and with Oriens, Paymon, Egyn, Amaymon: Samael E, Azazel W, Azael N, Mahazael S. Mathers' 1904 footnote follows the II.7 order. Only Samael (East) agrees under both readings; the other three follow II.7 at low confidence, with the alternative given in extra.

Agrippa chapter number (added when the data was merged): the goetic research cites Occult Philosophy III.24 for the four evil kings (Urieus/Oriens, Amaymon, Paymon, Egin) and their Hebrew names, while the angelic research cites III.18 for the same passage (and III.24 for the four princes of angels over the winds). One of the two chapter references for the evil kings is probably wrong; check the text before quoting a chapter. The directions do not depend on it.

Theurgia-Goetia azimuths are the literal 32-point values of the manuscript's names: East by South 101.25, South by East 168.75, South by West 191.25, West by South 258.75, West by North 281.25, North by West 348.75, North by East 11.25, East by North 78.75. The Theurgia text only says to face 'that point of the compass' where the king has his mansion, and nothing in it spaces the kings evenly. The even spacing comes from Trithemius' 16 winds; each affected entry gives the Trithemian 16-wind azimuth in extra. All 16 directions were confirmed against both the section openings and the conjurations in Peterson's Sloane 3825 transcription. The only discrepancy is Cabariel: the heading gives no point, Sl. 2731 says 'west & by North', and the conjuration says 'North & by West' (kept at medium).

Dropped: 'Royne (≈ Viné) under Egyn'. In the Folger V.b.26 transcription, Royne is item 48 of the Office of Spirits (MS p. 78) with no king or quarter, and he is not among Egin's twelve chief spirits (MS pp. 83-84).

Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26) at MS p. 73: Orience of the east, Paymon of the west, Amaymon of the south and Egine of the North. MS p. 74 says to turn to the South to receive Amaymon and to look to the North when calling Egyn, and pp. 81-84 repeat the kings with twelve chief spirits each (not entered as separate points). The Folger transcription is copyright 2015 (Peterson and Harms); only facts are used from it.

Sloane 3853 fol. 258r names four kings of the air: Oriens East, Paymon West, Amaymon South and Egim North. On the same page, Add. 36674 fol. 65r puts Scor, Algor and Sefon under Oriens (East), Partas and Gamor under Amamion (South), and Vmbra and Anaboth under Egin (North); these subordinates are not entered as separate points. Wikipedia says Sloane 3853 makes Leraje, Aim, Bune and Paymon kings of the N, S, E and W, citing a secondary edition; this does not appear in Peterson's transcription and was not included.

The kings' quarters vary widely by tradition. Amaymon is East in Weyer and in the Goetia (Observations, Invocation of the King, spirit 70, p. 59); South in Agrippa (II.7 and the kings' chapter), Oberon and Sloane 3853; and North in Liber 777 (by row). Paimon is West in Goetia spirit 9, the 1904 p. 59 footnote, Agrippa, Oberon and Sloane 3853; North ('Aquilonem versus') in Weyer's Latin, which Scot renders 'northwest'; and South in 777. Oriens is East everywhere. Egyn/Egin is North in Agrippa, Oberon and Sloane 3853, while 777 puts Ariton (Mathers' equivalent of Egyn) in the West.

Only 7 of the 72 Goetia spirits carry a direction in the 1904 text: 1, 2, 9, 13, 32, 33 and 70. For 32 and 33 it is derived from Amaymon; for 13 it is a wand gesture towards the South and East, plotted at SE 135°. Confirmed for 1-36 in source/research/crowley_1904_text.json and for 1-72 in the crowley field of data/lesserkey.json, where 37-72 were transcribed from the 1904 print. Decan-based directions for other spirits are modern and are not in the 1904 text.

Ritual facts: the 1904 Goetia says the triangle is to be placed toward the quarter the spirit belongs to. The footnote on p. 43 says the quarter the spirit is attributed to decides which of the four chief kings is invoked. The Theurgia-Goetia says to face the compass point of the king's mansion, and that for the 11 wandering princes the facing does not matter.

Pseudomonarchia daemonum first appeared in the 1577 (fifth) edition of Weyer's De praestigiis daemonum, not 1563. Its four-kings passage (Amoymon E, Gorson S, Zymymar N, Goap W) and the binding hours are in the closing section, which is Scot 1584 XV.3. The Latin wording could not be quoted directly; the directions are confirmed through Scot and secondary citations, and Scot's English is used in the entries.

The Heptameron's winds were verified in Turner's English (B. Rowe's transcription): Sunday North, Monday West ('the winde of the Moon'), Tuesday East, Wednesday Southwest, Thursday South, Friday West, Saturday Southwest. The Latin for Sunday (Boreas), Monday (Zephyrus) and Tuesday (Subsolanus) was confirmed in the Folger MS; the other Latin wind names come from T.S. 2002. The printed text calls these kings 'angels of the air', though they behave as fallen aerial spirits (the closing notes for each day call them 'Spirits of the Air', and some of their effects are malefic), so they are kept in both the goetic and the angelic lists.

When the Heptameron day begins: the Heptameron says that in every country and season the first hour of the day starts at sunrise. The compass therefore switches weekday at local sunrise (computed with h0 = -0.833°), not at midnight.

How the Heptameron places these beings: the King and his ministers are written in the four angles of the outermost circle. Standing in the circle, the operator first calls from the four parts the angels who govern the planets and days, then the angels who rule the air that day. So the listed wind is the Air Angels' governing wind, but the rite also places their names at all four angles. Wednesday and Thursday list only two ministers, and Friday lists four.

Thursday and Saturday have no angels for the four quarters. The text says no angels of the air are found above the fifth heaven, so on Thursday four short Latin prayers are said toward E/W/N/S, and Saturday reuses Thursday's prayers. Yet both days still name a King of the Air with ministers. This contradiction is in the text itself.

Heptameron text: Robert Turner's English (1655), from Benjamin Rowe's 2000 e-text, with the Sunday lists spot-checked against the 1655 page scans on Wikisource. Variant spellings in 'extra' come from Frater T.S.'s revision (Celephaïs Press, 2002), which follows the Latin of Agrippa's Opera c.1600. Peterson's edition could not be loaded in full, so spellings were not checked against Peterson. The separate entry 'Vel' was removed: 'Caluel. Vel. Laquel.' uses the Latin 'vel' = 'or', so Caluel and Laquel are probably one angel. Sunday East: Turner prints 'Gabriel', T.S. (from the Latin) reads 'Fabriel', so that entry is medium.

The four archangels are placed differently in each tradition. Agrippa III.24: Michael E, Raphael W, Gabriel N, Nariel/Uriel S (the II.7 table agrees by column). Golden Dawn LBRP (Liber O 1909; 777 col. LIX with quarters from col. LVII): Raphael E, Michael S, Gabriel W, Auriel N. Bamidbar Rabbah 2:10: Gabriel before (east), Michael right (south by Num. 2), Raphael with Ephraim (west), Uriel left (north). Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer 4 names no compass points and is not entered. The app shows these as separate sets.

Agrippa's scale of four pairs the elements and quarters as Fire–East, Air–West, Water–North, Earth–South. Agrippa's rulers of the elements (Seraph, Cherub, Tharsis, Ariel) get a quarter only by sharing a column in the II.7 table, so they are medium. 777 col. LX swaps two of them: Ariel rules Air and Kerub rules Earth.

Enochian Watchtower Kings: the Golden Dawn attribution as printed in Liber Chanokh (1912) is Plate IV East/Air (BATAIVAH), Plate V West/Water (RAAGIOSL), Plate VI North/Earth (ICZHHCAL), Plate VII South/Fire (EDLPRNAA); the invocations spell them BATAIVAH, RAAGIOSEL, IC-ZOD-HEH-CAL and EDELPERNA. Dee's own orientation is disputed: every reading puts ORO in the East; enochian.blog (12 Dec 2025) gives ORO E, MOR S, MPH W, OIP N, while the same author (20 Jan 2026) and Stenwick (2014, Tabula Recensa) give ORO E, MPH S, OIP W, MOR N. Any 'Dee' orientation should be labelled disputed.

Elements on the Enochian tablets: most accounts say Dee's records do not give the tablets elements and that the Golden Dawn added them. The Vision of the Four Watchtowers (20 June 1584; A True & Faithful Relation, 1659, pp. 168ff, seen only through secondary quotations) describes the East cloth as blood-red, the South lily-white, the West dragon-skin green and the North a very dark hair colour.

777 col. LVIII 'Supreme Elemental Kings' (Tahoeloj, Thahebyobeaatan, Ohooohatan, Thahaaothahe) are placed by 777's own quarter column, as spelled in the app's 777.json. 777 does not explain where these names come from, so they are medium.

Left out on purpose: Revelation 7:1 (four unnamed angels holding the winds), 1 Enoch (no confirmed named list by direction), the Heptameron's angels of the day and of the seasons (no direction), Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer 4 (positions around the Throne only), the Grimorium Verum (continents, not compass points) and Abramelin's sub-princes (no quarters).

Duplicates kept on purpose: the LBRP archangels and 777's rulers and angels of the elements appear in both the quarters and the angelic lists; the Heptameron kings of the air appear in both the goetic and the angelic lists; Agrippa's evil kings and princes of devils appear twice (the goetic variant set, and the angel-layer cross-reference stored here under goetic). The compass shows each set only when it is switched on.

Live placements are the app's computation, not textual attributions: the spirits and Shem angels of the rising decan are placed at the Ascendant's azimuth, and the decan pairing (from goetia.json) is a modern scheme, not in the 1904 Goetia.
