quarters.extra: אוריאל 'Light of God'; 'on my left hand'; archangel of Earth; Liber O and 777 spell it Auriel
quarters.note: Auriel is named at the left hand, which is North when facing East.
quarters.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909); Liber 777 (1909) col. LIX

quarters.name: Man — Aquarius
quarters.extra: ♒ 'sign of the head of the Man'; 777 col. XXXVIII (Air row) lists 'Eagle, Man (Cherub of Air)'
quarters.note: The Air-grade opening invokes toward the East using the sign of the Man's head (Aquarius).
quarters.source: GD 2=9 Theoricus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2); Liber 777 (1909) col. XXXVIII

quarters.name: Lion — Leo
quarters.extra: ♌ 'sign of the Lion'; 777 col. XXXVIII (Fire row): 'Lion (Cherub of Fire)'
quarters.note: The Fire-grade invocation toward the South uses the sign of the Lion.
quarters.source: GD 4=7 Philosophus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2); Liber 777 (1909) col. XXXVIII

quarters.name: Eagle — Scorpio
quarters.extra: ♏ 'sign of the Eagle'; 777 col. XXXVIII (Water row): 'Eagle-Snake-Scorpion (Cherub of Water)'
quarters.note: The Water-grade invocation toward the West uses the sign of the Eagle.
quarters.source: GD 3=8 Practicus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2); Liber 777 (1909) col. XXXVIII

quarters.name: Bull (Ox) — Taurus
quarters.extra: ♉ 'sign of the head of the Ox'; 777 col. XXXVIII (Taurus row): 'Bull (Cherub of Earth)'
quarters.note: The Earth-grade invocation toward the North uses the sign of the Ox's head, together with the name of Auriel.
quarters.source: GD 1=10 Zelator opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2); Liber 777 (1909) col. XXXVIII

quarters.name: Dagger
quarters.extra: 777 col. XLI (Air row): 'The Dagger or Fan'
quarters.note: In the Golden Dawn set of four elemental weapons, the Air Dagger belongs to the eastern quarter.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (Inner Order papers on the elemental weapons); Liber 777 (1909) col. XLI

quarters.name: Wand
quarters.extra: 777 col. XLI (Fire row): 'The Wand or Lamp, Pyramid of Fire'
quarters.note: The Fire Wand belongs to the southern quarter.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (elemental weapons); Liber 777 (1909) col. XLI

quarters.name: Cup
quarters.extra: 777 col. XLI (Water row): 'The Cup and Cross of Suffering, the Wine'
quarters.note: The Water Cup belongs to the western quarter.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (elemental weapons); Liber 777 (1909) col. XLI

quarters.name: Pentacle
quarters.extra: Crowley spells it 'Pantacle' (Book 4 Part II, 1913)
quarters.note: The Earth Pentacle belongs to the northern quarter.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (elemental weapons); Crowley, Book 4 Part II (1913)

quarters.name: Eurus
quarters.extra: Greek Εὖρος; Agrippa says it is also called Apeliotes; this is the wind's direction, not a GD element attribution
quarters.note: Agrippa describes the east wind as damp, cloudy and devouring, and sets it against Zephyrus.
quarters.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1533; J.F. trans. 1651), Bk I ch. 6 'Of the wonderful natures of Water, Air, and Winds'

quarters.name: Notus
quarters.extra: Greek Νότος; Latin Auster
quarters.note: Agrippa's south wind is warm, wet, cloudy and unhealthy, and it brings the rains.
quarters.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk I ch. 6

quarters.name: Zephyrus
quarters.extra: Greek Ζέφυρος; Latin Favonius
quarters.note: Agrippa's west wind is the gentle one that ends winter and brings out leaves and flowers.
quarters.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk I ch. 6

quarters.name: Boreas
quarters.extra: Greek Βορέας; Latin Aquilo
quarters.note: Agrippa's north wind is violent: it drives off clouds, clears the sky and freezes water.
quarters.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk I ch. 6

quarters.name: Paralda
quarters.extra: 777 col. LXII 'Kings of the Elemental Spirits'; the same names occur in Éliphas Lévi
quarters.note: Paralda rules the spirits of Air, and so of the eastern quarter.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXII; cf. Lévi, Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie (1856)

quarters.name: Djin
quarters.extra: 777 col. LXII
quarters.note: Djin rules the spirits of Fire in the southern quarter.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXII; cf. Lévi (1856)

quarters.name: Niksa
quarters.extra: 777 col. LXII; also spelled Nichsa or Nicksa
quarters.note: Niksa rules the spirits of Water in the western quarter.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXII; cf. Lévi (1856)

quarters.name: Ghob
quarters.extra: 777 col. LXII; also spelled Gob
quarters.note: Ghob rules the spirits of Earth in the northern quarter.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXII; cf. Lévi (1856)

quarters.name: Sylphs
quarters.extra: 777 col. CLXXXIII 'Legendary Orders of Being'
quarters.note: Sylphs are Paracelsus's spirits of Air; through the Air–East attribution they belong to the East.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. CLXXXIII and LVII; Paracelsus, Liber de nymphis, sylphis, pygmaeis et salamandris (1566)

quarters.name: Salamanders
quarters.extra: 777 col. CLXXXIII
quarters.note: Salamanders are the spirits of Fire and belong to the South.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. CLXXXIII and LVII; Paracelsus (1566)

quarters.name: Undines
quarters.extra: 777: 'Nymphs and Undines, Nereids, &c.'
quarters.note: Undines and nymphs are the spirits of Water and belong to the West.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. CLXXXIII and LVII; Paracelsus (1566)

quarters.name: Gnomes
quarters.extra: 777 col. CLXXXIII, listed with 'The Dweller of the Threshold'
quarters.note: Gnomes (Paracelsus's pygmies) are the spirits of Earth and belong to the North.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. CLXXXIII and LVII; Paracelsus (1566)

quarters.name: Yellow / violet
quarters.extra: Air tablet: yellow with violet letters; 777 King scale for Air: bright pale yellow (col. XV)
quarters.note: Air is shown in yellow against its complement, violet, so that the colours seem to flash.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (Llewellyn 6th ed., 1989) p. 479, as cited in Wikipedia 'Watchtower (magic)'; Liber 777 col. XV

quarters.name: Red / green
quarters.extra: Fire tablet: red with green letters; 777 King scale for Fire: glowing orange scarlet
quarters.note: Fire is shown in red against its complement, green.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (1989) p. 479, via Wikipedia 'Watchtower (magic)'; Liber 777 col. XV

quarters.name: Blue / orange
quarters.extra: Water tablet: blue with orange letters; 777 King scale for Water: deep blue
quarters.note: Water is shown in blue against its complement, orange.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (1989) p. 479, via Wikipedia 'Watchtower (magic)'; Liber 777 col. XV

quarters.name: Black / green (variants)
quarters.extra: variants: black/white, or 777 col. XV for Earth: 'Citrine, russet, olive & black (quartered)'
quarters.note: Wikipedia's reading of Regardie gives the Earth tablet as black with green letters, but sources differ and black has no true complementary colour.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (1989) p. 479, via Wikipedia 'Watchtower (magic)'; Liber 777 col. XV

quarters.name: Ariel
quarters.extra: אריאל
quarters.note: Liber 777 makes Ariel the ruler of Air, and so of the eastern quarter; Agrippa gives Ariel to Earth instead.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LX 'The Rulers of the Elements'

quarters.name: Seraph
quarters.extra: שרף
quarters.note: Seraph rules Fire in the South.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LX

quarters.name: Tharsis
quarters.extra: תרשיס
quarters.note: Tharsis rules Water in the West.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LX

quarters.name: Kerub
quarters.extra: כרוב
quarters.note: Kerub rules Earth in the North; Agrippa gives Cherub to Air instead.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LX

quarters.name: Chassan
quarters.extra: חסן
quarters.note: Liber 777 makes Chassan the angel of Air.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXI 'Angels of the Elements'

quarters.name: Aral
quarters.extra: אראל
quarters.note: Liber 777 makes Aral the angel of Fire.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXI

quarters.name: Taliahad
quarters.extra: printed תליהד in 777 (GD spelling טליהד)
quarters.note: Liber 777 makes Taliahad the angel of Water.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXI

quarters.name: Phorlakh
quarters.extra: פורלאך
quarters.note: Liber 777 makes Phorlakh the angel of Earth.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXI

quarters.name: Shaddai El Chai
quarters.extra: שדי אל חי 'Almighty Living God'; Theoricus 2=9
quarters.note: The Air-grade opening faces East and invokes under this name, with Raphael as archangel.
quarters.source: GD 2=9 Theoricus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2, 1937)

quarters.name: YHVH Tzabaoth
quarters.extra: יהוה צבאות 'Lord of Hosts' (the ritual says 'Tetragrammaton Tzabaoth'); Philosophus 4=7
quarters.note: The Fire-grade opening faces South and invokes under this name, with Michael as archangel.
quarters.source: GD 4=7 Philosophus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

quarters.name: Elohim Tzabaoth
quarters.extra: אלהים צבאות 'God of Hosts'; Practicus 3=8
quarters.note: The Water-grade opening faces West and invokes under this name, with Gabriel as archangel.
quarters.source: GD 3=8 Practicus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

quarters.name: Adonai ha-Aretz / Adonai Melekh
quarters.extra: אדני הארץ 'Lord of the Earth', אדני מלך 'Lord and King'; Adonai Melekh is the name used in the actual invocation; Zelator 1=10
quarters.note: The Earth-grade opening faces North, adores under Adonai ha-Aretz and Adonai Melekh, and invokes with Auriel as archangel.
quarters.source: GD 1=10 Zelator opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

quarters.name: Tablet of Air (EXARP)
quarters.extra: EXARP is its line of the Tablet of Union; three holy names ORO IBAH AOZPI; Great King BATAIVAH ('Great King of the East' in the 2=9)
quarters.note: The Golden Dawn sets Dee's Air tablet in the East, and its names are invoked in the Theoricus opening.
quarters.source: GD 2=9 Theoricus opening; Regardie, The Golden Dawn (Enochian papers, SIRP); Crowley, Liber Chanokh (Equinox I:7–8, 1912)

quarters.name: Tablet of Fire (BITOM)
quarters.extra: three holy names OIP TEAA PEDOCE (OIP TEAA PDOCE); Great King EDLPRNAA ('Edelperna, Great King of the South' in the 4=7)
quarters.note: The Fire tablet is set in the South, and its names are invoked in the Philosophus opening.
quarters.source: GD 4=7 Philosophus opening; Regardie, The Golden Dawn; Liber Chanokh (1912)

quarters.name: Tablet of Water (HCOMA)
quarters.extra: three holy names EMPEH ARSEL GAIOL (MPH ARSL GAIOL); Great King RAAGIOSL ('Ra-agiosel, Great King of the West' in the 3=8)
quarters.note: The Water tablet is set in the West, and its names are invoked in the Practicus opening.
quarters.source: GD 3=8 Practicus opening; Regardie, The Golden Dawn; Liber Chanokh (1912)

quarters.name: Tablet of Earth (NANTA)
quarters.extra: three holy names EMOR DIAL HECTEGA (MOR DIAL HCTGA); Great King ICZHIHAL ('Ic Zod Heh Chal, Great King of the North' in the 1=10)
quarters.note: The Earth tablet is set in the North, and its names are invoked in the Zelator opening.
quarters.source: GD 1=10 Zelator opening; Regardie, The Golden Dawn; Liber Chanokh (1912)

quarters.name: YHVH (Air pentagram)
quarters.role: divine name of the elemental pentagram
quarters.group: Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram (Golden Dawn)
quarters.extra: active Spirit pentagram: EXARP + Eheieh אהיה; then Air pentagram: ORO IBAH AOZPI + YHVH; sign of Aquarius
quarters.note: In the Supreme ritual the East gets an active Spirit pentagram and then an Air pentagram charged with YHVH.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn, 'Supreme Invoking Ritual of the Pentagram' (Inner Order material as arranged by Regardie)

quarters.name: Elohim (Fire pentagram)
quarters.role: divine name of the elemental pentagram
quarters.group: Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram (Golden Dawn)
quarters.extra: active Spirit pentagram: BITOM + Eheieh; then Fire pentagram: OIP TEAA PEDOCE + אלהים Elohim; sign of Leo
quarters.note: The South gets an active Spirit pentagram and then a Fire pentagram charged with Elohim.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn, 'Supreme Invoking Ritual of the Pentagram'

quarters.name: El (Water pentagram)
quarters.role: divine name of the elemental pentagram
quarters.group: Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram (Golden Dawn)
quarters.extra: passive Spirit pentagram: HCOMA + AGLA אגלא; then Water pentagram: EMPEH ARSEL GAIOL + אל El; eagle's-head sign
quarters.note: The West gets a passive Spirit pentagram and then a Water pentagram charged with El.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn, 'Supreme Invoking Ritual of the Pentagram'

quarters.name: Adonai (Earth pentagram)
quarters.role: divine name of the elemental pentagram
quarters.group: Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram (Golden Dawn)
quarters.extra: passive Spirit pentagram: NANTA + AGLA; then Earth pentagram: EMOR DIAL HECTEGA + אדני Adonai (some versions Adonai ha-Aretz); sign of Taurus
quarters.note: The North gets a passive Spirit pentagram and then an Earth pentagram charged with Adonai.
quarters.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn, 'Supreme Invoking Ritual of the Pentagram'

quarters.name: Hexagram of Fire
quarters.group: Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram (Liber O)
quarters.extra: ARARITA is said; an elemental form, not a planet (zodiacal quarters: Aries East)
quarters.note: Liber O traces the Fire form of the hexagram in the East, so the hexagram's quarters differ from the pentagram's.
quarters.source: Crowley, Liber O vel Manus et Sagittae (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram

quarters.name: Hexagram of Earth
quarters.group: Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram (Liber O)
quarters.extra: ARARITA
quarters.note: The Earth form of the hexagram is traced in the South.
quarters.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram

quarters.name: Hexagram of Air
quarters.group: Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram (Liber O)
quarters.extra: ARARITA
quarters.note: The Air form of the hexagram is traced in the West.
quarters.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram

quarters.name: Hexagram of Water
quarters.group: Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram (Liber O)
quarters.extra: ARARITA
quarters.note: The Water form of the hexagram is traced in the North.
quarters.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram

quarters.name: Hierophant
quarters.extra: Throne of the East; the rising of the Sun of Life and Light
quarters.note: The Hierophant rules from the Throne of the East, which stands for the rising of the Sun of Life and Light.
quarters.source: GD 0=0 Neophyte ritual, opening (printed in The Equinox I:2, 1909; Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

quarters.name: Dadouchos
quarters.extra: torch-bearer; censer, purification by Fire; heat and dryness
quarters.note: The Dadouchos stands in the South, standing for heat and dryness, and purifies with fire.
quarters.source: GD 0=0 Neophyte ritual, opening (Equinox I:2, 1909; Regardie vol. 2)

quarters.name: Hiereus
quarters.extra: Throne of the West; increase of darkness, decrease of light
quarters.note: The Hiereus sits on the Throne of the West, the place where darkness grows and light wanes.
quarters.source: GD 0=0 Neophyte ritual, opening (Equinox I:2, 1909; Regardie vol. 2)

quarters.name: Stolistes
quarters.extra: cup of lustral water, purification by Water; cold and moisture; the North is 'the place of greatest symbolic darkness'
quarters.note: The Stolistes stands in the North, standing for cold and moisture. After the obligation the candidate is led to the North, the darkest part of the Hall.
quarters.source: GD 0=0 Neophyte ritual (Equinox I:2, 1909; Regardie vol. 2)

quarters.name: Michael
quarters.role: angel ruling a corner of the world
quarters.group: Agrippa — Scale of the Number Four (variant)
quarters.extra: same column: Fire; ruler Seraph; animal Lion
quarters.note: Agrippa's table puts Michael in the same column as the East and Fire, whereas the Golden Dawn gives Michael the South.
quarters.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1533; J.F. trans. 1651), Bk II ch. 7, Scale of the Number Four

quarters.name: Uriel
quarters.role: angel ruling a corner of the world
quarters.group: Agrippa — Scale of the Number Four (variant)
quarters.extra: same column: Earth (עפר); ruler Ariel; animal Calf
quarters.note: Agrippa puts Uriel in the same column as the South and Earth.
quarters.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk II ch. 7

quarters.name: Raphael
quarters.role: angel ruling a corner of the world
quarters.group: Agrippa — Scale of the Number Four (variant)
quarters.extra: same column: Air; ruler Cherub; animal Eagle
quarters.note: Agrippa puts Raphael in the same column as the West and Air.
quarters.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk II ch. 7

quarters.name: Gabriel
quarters.role: angel ruling a corner of the world
quarters.group: Agrippa — Scale of the Number Four (variant)
quarters.extra: same column: Water; ruler Tharsis; animal Man
quarters.note: Agrippa puts Gabriel in the same column as the North and Water.
quarters.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk II ch. 7

quarters.name: Tiphareth
quarters.extra: תפארת; in the same column Chesed = Height and Geburah = Depth
quarters.note: Liber 777 maps the six sealed directions of the Sepher Yetzirah onto Sephiroth 4–9, which gives the East to Tiphareth.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. CX 'Elements and Quarters (Sepher Yetzirah)', after Sepher Yetzirah 1:13

quarters.name: Hod
quarters.extra: הוד
quarters.note: In the same table, Hod is the South.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. CX

quarters.name: Netzach
quarters.extra: נצח
quarters.note: In the same table, Netzach is the West.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. CX

quarters.name: Yesod
quarters.extra: יסוד
quarters.note: In the same table, Yesod is the North.
quarters.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. CX

thelema.name: Ra
thelema.extra: sunrise; Ra 'in Thy rising' and 'in Thy strength'; the Sun's bark comes 'from the Abodes of Night'
thelema.note: At dawn the aspirant faces East, gives the sign of his grade and hails the Sun as Ra.
thelema.source: Crowley, Liber Resh vel Helios sub figura CC §1 (The Equinox I:6, 1911)

thelema.name: Ahathoor
thelema.extra: noon; 'in Thy triumphing' and 'in Thy beauty'; 'from the Abodes of Morning'
thelema.note: At noon the aspirant faces South and hails the Sun as Ahathoor (Hathor).
thelema.source: Liber Resh vel Helios §2 (Equinox I:6, 1911)

thelema.name: Tum
thelema.extra: sunset; 'in Thy setting' and 'in Thy joy'; 'from the Abodes of Day'
thelema.note: At sunset the aspirant faces West and hails the Sun as Tum (Atum).
thelema.source: Liber Resh vel Helios §3 (Equinox I:6, 1911)

thelema.name: Khephra
thelema.extra: midnight; 'in Thy hiding' and 'in Thy silence'; 'from the Abodes of Evening'; the app's data/resh.json spells it 'Khepra'
thelema.note: At midnight the aspirant faces North and hails the hidden Sun as Khephra (Khepri).
thelema.source: Liber Resh vel Helios §4 (Equinox I:6, 1911)

thelema.name: ΧΑΟΣ (Chaos)
thelema.extra: roared; 1st station; the circuit is widdershins E→N→W→S
thelema.note: Advancing to the East, the operator projects the pentagram with the sign of Horus and roars Chaos.
thelema.source: Crowley, The Book of Lies (Wieland, 1913), ch. 25 (ΚΕ) 'The Star Ruby'

thelema.name: ΒΑΒΑΛΟΝ (Babalon)
thelema.extra: screamed; 2nd station
thelema.note: Going widdershins to the North, the operator repeats the gesture and screams Babalon.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913), ch. 25

thelema.name: ΕΡΩΣ (Eros)
thelema.extra: said; 3rd station
thelema.note: In the West the gesture is repeated and Eros is spoken.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913), ch. 25

thelema.name: ΨΥΧΗ (Psyche)
thelema.extra: bellowed; 4th station
thelema.note: In the South the operator bellows Psyche, then completes the circle and returns to the centre.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913), ch. 25

thelema.name: ΘΗΡΙΟΝ (Therion)
thelema.extra: roared; replaces ΧΑΟΣ; the only one of the four new names printed in Greek; widdershins circuit
thelema.note: In the revised rite the East pentagram is charged with Therion, the Beast.
thelema.source: Crowley, Magick in Theory and Practice (Paris: Lecram, 1929), Appendix VI, Liber XXV

thelema.name: NUIT
thelema.extra: said; replaces ΒΑΒΑΛΟΝ; printed in Roman capitals
thelema.note: In the revision the North takes Nuit, and Babalon moves to the West.
thelema.source: Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), App. VI, Liber XXV (collated in the O.T.O./Celephaïs e-text footnotes)

thelema.name: BABALON
thelema.extra: whispered; replaces ΕΡΩΣ
thelema.note: In the revision the West takes Babalon, whispered.
thelema.source: Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), App. VI, Liber XXV

thelema.name: HADIT
thelema.extra: bellowed; replaces ΨΥΧΗ
thelema.note: In the revision the South takes Hadit, bellowed.
thelema.source: Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), App. VI, Liber XXV

thelema.name: Iynges (ΙΥΓΓΕΣ)
thelema.extra: ΠΡΟ ΜΟΥ ΙΥΓΓΕΣ
thelema.note: Standing in the centre with arms in a Tau, the operator places the Iynges in front of him. That is East if he faces East there, as he does at the start and end of the rite.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 25; MTP (1929) App. VI; the terms come from the Chaldean Oracles

thelema.name: Teletarchae (ΤΕΛΕΤΑΡΧΑΙ)
thelema.extra: ΟΠΙΣΩ ΜΟΥ ΤΕΛΕΤΑΡΧΑΙ
thelema.note: The Teletarchs are placed behind the operator, which is West when facing East.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 25; MTP (1929) App. VI

thelema.name: Synoches (ΣΥΝΟΧΕΣ)
thelema.role: Chaldean-Oracle power — on my right hand
thelema.extra: ΕΠΙ ΔΕΞΙΑ ΣΥΝΟΧΕΣ
thelema.note: The Synoches are at the right hand, which is South when facing East.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 25; MTP (1929) App. VI

thelema.name: Daimones (ΔΑΙΜΟΝΕΣ)
thelema.extra: ΕΠΑΡΙΣΤΕΡΑ ΔΑΙΜΟΝΕΣ
thelema.note: The daimons are at the left hand, which is North when facing East.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 25; MTP (1929) App. VI

thelema.name: Boleskine — facing
thelema.note: The Magician begins by turning to face Boleskine, which the text calls the House of the Beast 666, and projects the force radiating from it as he circles.
thelema.source: Crowley, Liber V vel Reguli, First Gesture (Magick in Theory and Practice, 1929, App. VI); coordinates from OS NGR NH 50847 22116 (Buildings at Risk Register) converted to WGS84

thelema.name: Nuit
thelema.extra: averse pentagram invoking Air (Aquarius); sign Puella; 1st station, reached by turning to the left (widdershins)
thelema.note: In the Enchantment the Magician halts in the North, traces the averse Air pentagram and calls on Nuit.
thelema.source: Liber V vel Reguli, Second Gesture 'The Enchantment' (MTP 1929, App. VI)

thelema.name: Hadit
thelema.extra: averse pentagram invoking Fire (Leo); sign Puer; 2nd station
thelema.note: Halting next in the South, he traces the averse Fire pentagram and cries Hadit.
thelema.source: Liber V vel Reguli, Second Gesture (MTP 1929, App. VI)

thelema.name: Therion
thelema.extra: averse pentagram invoking Earth (Taurus); sign Vir; 3rd station
thelema.note: In the East he traces the averse Earth pentagram and cries Therion.
thelema.source: Liber V vel Reguli, Second Gesture (MTP 1929, App. VI)

thelema.name: Babalon
thelema.extra: averse pentagram invoking Water (no zodiac sign named); sign Mulier; 4th station
thelema.note: In the West he traces the averse Water pentagram and calls on Babalon.
thelema.source: Liber V vel Reguli, Second Gesture (MTP 1929, App. VI)

thelema.name: Boleskine House (Temple East / High Altar)
thelema.note: Liber XV defines the temple's East as the direction of Boleskine, on the south-eastern shore of Loch Ness two miles east of Foyers. The High Altar stands there, the small altar and font are in the middle, and the Tomb is at the West end.
thelema.source: Crowley, Liber XV, Ecclesiae Gnosticae Catholicae Canon Missae §I (The International, 1918; Equinox III:1, 1919); coordinates from OS NGR NH 50847 22116 converted to WGS84 (Wikipedia gives 57.2653°N 4.4747°W)

thelema.name: Section B — Air
thelema.extra: opening barbarous names AR ThIAF RhEIBET…; golden light; from here the Adept circles widdershins (astrally)
thelema.note: Crowley's explanation of the ritual has the Adept invoke Air in the East, sending out a shaft of golden light.
thelema.source: Crowley, Liber Samekh, Point II explanatory notes, Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), Appendix IV

thelema.name: Section C — Fire
thelema.extra: opening names AR-O-GO-GO-RU-ABRAO SOTOU…; flame-red rays
thelema.note: The Adept next invokes Fire in the South, with red flame streaming from him.
thelema.source: Liber Samekh, Point II notes (MTP 1929, App. IV)

thelema.name: Section D — Water
thelema.extra: opening names RU-ABRA-IAF MRIODOM…; blue radiance
thelema.note: He invokes Water in the West, and his wand pours out blue light.
thelema.source: Liber Samekh, Point II notes (MTP 1929, App. IV)

thelema.name: Section E — Earth
thelema.extra: opening names MA BARRAIO IOEL…; green flame
thelema.note: He goes to the North to invoke Earth, with green fire flashing from his weapon.
thelema.source: Liber Samekh, Point II notes (MTP 1929, App. IV)

thelema.name: Section F — Spirit (toward Boleskine)
thelema.extra: 57.2653,-4.4748; active pentagrams, the Mark of the Beast and the L.V.X. signs; opening names AFT ABAFT BAS-AUMGN…
thelema.note: For Spirit, the Adept goes back to the centre and invokes facing Boleskine, using the active pentagrams and the Mark of the Beast.
thelema.source: Liber Samekh, Point II notes (MTP 1929, App. IV)

thelema.name: Pater et Mater unus deus Ararita
thelema.extra: Holy Hexagram; 1st station; deosil circuit E→S→W→N; the 1913 text prints 'UNIS' at this station
thelema.note: From the centre the adept goes to the East, makes the Holy Hexagram and proclaims Father and Mother as one god, Ararita.
thelema.source: Crowley, The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 36 'The Star Sapphire'; reprinted in MTP (1929) App. VI

thelema.name: Mater et Filius unus deus Ararita
thelema.extra: Holy Hexagram; 2nd station
thelema.note: In the South the hexagram is made with the formula of Mother and Son.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 36; MTP (1929) App. VI

thelema.name: Filius et Filia unus deus Ararita
thelema.extra: Holy Hexagram; 3rd station
thelema.note: In the West the hexagram is made with the formula of Son and Daughter.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 36; MTP (1929) App. VI

thelema.name: Filia et Pater unus deus Ararita
thelema.extra: Holy Hexagram; 4th station
thelema.note: In the North the hexagram is made with the formula of Daughter and Father, and then the adept returns to the centre.
thelema.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 36; MTP (1929) App. VI

goetic.name: Amaymon
goetic.role: king of the East (first of the four great kings)
goetic.group: Four Kings of the quarters — Goetia 1904
goetic.extra: 1904 print spellings: AMAYMON (Observations p. 31; spirits 13, 32, 33, 70) and AMAIMON (Invocation of the King p. 43; Enochian 'Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge' p. 59). Spirits named as his: 32 Asmoday, 33 Gäap, 70 Seere.
goetic.note: First of the four great kings over the 72, and the only one whose quarter the text states outright. The Invocation of the King addresses him as ruler in the Dominion of the East, and Seere's entry calls him King of the East. The kings are invoked to send their spirits and are called forth themselves only on great occasions.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904): Observations p. 31; The Invocation of the King p. 43 and its footnote; Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge p. 59; spirit 70 (checked against the scan of the 1904 printing on Wikimedia Commons)

goetic.name: Corson
goetic.role: king (one of the four great kings)
goetic.group: Four Kings of the quarters — Goetia 1904
goetic.extra: 1904 print p. 31: CORSON. Weyer/Scot: Gorson, King of the SOUTH. Crowley's footnote on p. 59 of the same edition names Paimon, not Corson, for the West. Not the same as spirit 20 Purson.
goetic.note: Second of the four kings in the list, which the text follows with 'East, West, North, and South'. West comes only from reading the two lists in order.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), Observations p. 31

goetic.name: Ziminiar (Zimimay)
goetic.role: king (one of the four great kings)
goetic.group: Four Kings of the quarters — Goetia 1904
goetic.extra: 1904 print p. 31: ZIMIMAY or ZIMINIAR; p. 59 footnote: Zodimay (North by order). de Laurence 1916: ZIMIMAY or ZIMINAIR. Weyer: Zymymar. Scot: Zimimar.
goetic.note: Third of the four kings. Reading the lists in order makes him King of the North, and both Weyer and Crowley's Zodimay footnote agree.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), Observations p. 31 and footnote p. 59; cf. Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577), closing section

goetic.name: Göap
goetic.role: king (one of the four great kings)
goetic.group: Four Kings of the quarters — Goetia 1904
goetic.extra: 1904 print p. 31: GÖAP (the 2003 Celephaïs re-set prints GOAP). Crowley's p. 59 footnote puts 'Gaap' in the South position. Weyer: Goap, king and prince of the WEST. In the Observations he is distinct from spirit 33 Gäap.
goetic.note: Fourth of the four kings. South comes from reading the lists in order, and Crowley's Enochian invocation in the same edition also pairs a 'Gaap' with the South. Weyer, the older source of this passage, makes Goap king of the West.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), Observations p. 31; Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge, footnote p. 59

goetic.name: Amaimon
goetic.role: king of the East (default king of the invocation)
goetic.group: Four Kings — Crowley's Enochian invocation (Goetia 1904 p. 59)
goetic.extra: The English line reads 'kingdoms of the East' followed by '(South, West, North)' in brackets. Footnote on his name: Gaap, Paimon, Zodimay.
goetic.note: Crowley's Angelic-language version of the Invocation of the King addresses Amaimon as ruling in the kingdoms of the East, with the other three quarters in brackets as alternatives.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), 'Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge', p. 59 (1904 print scan, Wikimedia Commons)

goetic.name: Gaap
goetic.role: king invoked for the South (alternative to Amaimon)
goetic.group: Four Kings — Crowley's Enochian invocation (Goetia 1904 p. 59)
goetic.extra: Footnote: 'Or Gaap, Paimon, Zodimay, as the case may be.' Gaap stands where the Observations list GÖAP; spirit 33 is spelled Gäap.
goetic.note: The footnote gives three substitutes for Amaimon in the same order as the bracketed South, West and North, which pairs Gaap with the South.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), footnote to 'Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge', p. 59

goetic.name: Paimon
goetic.role: king invoked for the West (alternative to Amaimon)
goetic.group: Four Kings — Crowley's Enochian invocation (Goetia 1904 p. 59)
goetic.extra: Agrees with spirit 9 (observed towards the West) and with Agrippa, Oberon and Sloane 3853. Replaces Corson of the Observations.
goetic.note: Paimon is the second substitute in the footnote, matched by order to the West.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), footnote p. 59

goetic.name: Zodimay
goetic.role: king invoked for the North (alternative to Amaimon)
goetic.group: Four Kings — Crowley's Enochian invocation (Goetia 1904 p. 59)
goetic.extra: The same king as the Observations' Zimimay/Ziminiar.
goetic.note: Zodimay is the third substitute in the footnote, matched by order to the North.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), footnote p. 59

goetic.name: Bael
goetic.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: spirit 1. Weyer/Scot: 'of the power of the east'.
goetic.note: The first principal spirit, a king ruling in the East.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 1

goetic.name: Agares
goetic.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: spirit 2; variant Agreas. Weyer/Scot: first duke under the power of the east.
goetic.note: A duke under the power of the East.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 2

goetic.name: Paimon
goetic.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: spirit 9. Weyer: faces Aquilo (north); Scot: 'northwest'. Crowley's 1904 footnote (p. 59) also makes Paimon the king for the West.
goetic.note: The text says he is to be observed towards the West. Weyer has the exorcist face north instead.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 9

goetic.name: Beleth
goetic.role: king (ritual gesture towards South and East)
goetic.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: spirit 13. Weyer/Scot (Byleth): the rod is held toward the east and south. The silver ring is held to the face 'as before AMAYMON'.
goetic.note: To handle him, the exorcist strikes a hazel wand out towards the South and East quarters and draws a triangle outside the circle. The point is plotted at the south-east midpoint.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 13

goetic.name: Asmoday
goetic.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: spirit 32. His 72 legions are counted among Amaymon's. In Oberon, Asmoday heads Amaymon's twelve, but there Amaymon is King of the South.
goetic.note: First and choicest under the power of Amaymon, going before all the others. East is derived from Amaymon's stated quarter, since the entry itself names no direction.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 32

goetic.name: Gäap
goetic.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: spirit 33. Appears 'when the Sun is in some of the Southern Signs', which is zodiacal and not a compass point. Crowley's 1904 footnote (p. 59) names a 'Gaap' as the king for the SOUTH.
goetic.note: He teaches how to consecrate things of the dominion of Amaymon, whom the text calls his King, so East is derived from that. The same edition's Enochian-invocation footnote treats Gaap as the southern king, so the two readings conflict.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 33; footnote p. 59

goetic.name: Seere
goetic.role: prince under Amaymon, King of the East
goetic.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: spirit 70; variants Sear, Seir. Not in Weyer. Checked against the 1904 print (lesserkey.json crowley field).
goetic.note: A mighty prince under Amaymon, whom this entry explicitly calls King of the East.
goetic.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 70

goetic.name: Amoymon (Amaymon)
goetic.group: Variant kings — Pseudomonarchia daemonum (Weyer 1577 / Scot 1584)
goetic.extra: Scot: Amaymon king of the east
goetic.note: The closing section on binding hours names him King of the East. The four kings may be bound from the third hour until noon and from the ninth hour until evening.
goetic.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (appendix to De praestigiis daemonum, 1577), closing section; Scot, Discoverie of Witchcraft (1584) XV.3

goetic.name: Gorson
goetic.group: Variant kings — Pseudomonarchia daemonum (Weyer 1577 / Scot 1584)
goetic.extra: Goetia form: Corson
goetic.note: King of the South in Weyer's list, where the Goetia's list order puts Corson in the West.
goetic.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577), closing section; Scot (1584) XV.3

goetic.name: Zymymar (Zimimar)
goetic.group: Variant kings — Pseudomonarchia daemonum (Weyer 1577 / Scot 1584)
goetic.extra: Scot: Zimimar; Goetia: Zimimay/Ziminiar
goetic.note: King of the North, which agrees with the Goetia.
goetic.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577), closing section; Scot (1584) XV.3

goetic.name: Goap
goetic.role: king and prince of the West
goetic.group: Variant kings — Pseudomonarchia daemonum (Weyer 1577 / Scot 1584)
goetic.extra: Goetia 1904: GÖAP (South by list order)
goetic.note: King and prince of the West in Weyer, where the Goetia's list order puts Göap in the South.
goetic.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577), closing section; Scot (1584) XV.3

goetic.name: Baël
goetic.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: Weyer §1; = Goetia spirit 1
goetic.note: The first king, of the power of the East.
goetic.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §1; Scot (1584) XV.2

goetic.name: Agares
goetic.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: Weyer §2; = Goetia spirit 2
goetic.note: The first duke under the power of the East.
goetic.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §2; Scot (1584) XV.2

goetic.name: Byleth
goetic.role: king (ritual gesture towards East and South)
goetic.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: Weyer §20; = Goetia spirit 13 Beleth
goetic.note: The exorcist reaches a hazel rod out towards the East and South and makes a triangle beside the circle. The point is plotted at the south-east midpoint.
goetic.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §20; Scot (1584) XV.2

goetic.name: Paymon
goetic.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: Weyer §22. Latin 'Aquilonem versus' (Aquilo = the north wind); Scot's English: 'northwest'; Goetia spirit 9 says West.
goetic.note: When calling him, the exorcist looks towards Aquilo, the north wind, because his dwelling is there.
goetic.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §22; Scot (1584) XV.2

goetic.name: Sydonay alias Asmoday
goetic.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
goetic.extra: Weyer §35; = Goetia spirit 32
goetic.note: He goes before the others who are under Amaymon's power. East is derived from Amaymon's quarter in Weyer.
goetic.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §35; Scot (1584) XV.2

goetic.name: Urieus (Oriens)
goetic.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
goetic.extra: III.24 spelling: Urieus. II.7 'Scale of the number four': Oriens, in the same column as Fire and 'The East'.
goetic.note: One of four most mischievous kings set over the four parts of the world. Agrippa names him King of the East, and his table of fours puts Oriens in the East column.
goetic.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) III ch. 24 and II ch. 7; Eng. tr. J. F[reake] 1651

goetic.name: Amaymon
goetic.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
goetic.extra: In both III.24 and the II.7 table (Earth / South column). Contradicts the Goetia and Weyer, which put him in the East.
goetic.note: Agrippa makes Amaymon King of the South in both places.
goetic.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) III ch. 24 and II ch. 7; Eng. tr. 1651

goetic.name: Paymon
goetic.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
goetic.extra: In III.24 and the II.7 table (Air / West column). Agrees with Goetia spirit 9.
goetic.note: Agrippa makes Paymon King of the West.
goetic.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) III ch. 24 and II ch. 7; Eng. tr. 1651

goetic.name: Egin (Egyn)
goetic.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
goetic.extra: III.24: Egin; II.7 table: Egyn (Water / North column). Mathers' 1904 footnote equates Egyn with Ariton.
goetic.note: Agrippa makes Egin King of the North.
goetic.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) III ch. 24 and II ch. 7; Eng. tr. 1651

goetic.name: Samael (Samuel)
goetic.role: Hebrew name for the king of the East; prince of devils (Fire)
goetic.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
goetic.extra: III.24 (1651): 'Samuel'; II.7 table: Samael, in the Fire / East column. Both placements give East.
goetic.note: Agrippa gives the Hebrew doctors' names for the four kings with a hedge ('perhaps'). Samael falls in the East whether the names are matched by list order (III.24) or by the table's columns (II.7).
goetic.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) II ch. 7 (Scale of Four) and III ch. 24; Eng. tr. 1651

goetic.name: Azazel
goetic.role: prince of devils (Air); Hebrew name of a quarter-king
goetic.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
goetic.extra: II.7 table: Azazel in the Air / West column, under Paymon. III.24 list order would give SOUTH (matched to Amaymon).
goetic.note: In Agrippa's table of fours Azazel stands in the West column with Paymon. The order of the III.24 list would instead pair him with Amaymon in the South.
goetic.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) II ch. 7 (Scale of Four); cf. III ch. 24; Eng. tr. 1651

goetic.name: Azael
goetic.role: prince of devils (Water); Hebrew name of a quarter-king
goetic.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
goetic.extra: II.7 table: Azael in the Water / North column, under Egyn. III.24 list order would give WEST (matched to Paymon).
goetic.note: In the table of fours Azael shares the North column with Egyn. The III.24 order would pair him with Paymon in the West.
goetic.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) II ch. 7 (Scale of Four); cf. III ch. 24; Eng. tr. 1651

goetic.name: Mahazael (Mahazuel)
goetic.role: prince of devils (Earth); Hebrew name of a quarter-king
goetic.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
goetic.extra: III.24 (1651): 'Mahazuel'. II.7 table: Mahazael in the Earth / South column, under Amaymon. III.24 list order would give NORTH (matched to Egin).
goetic.note: In the table of fours Mahazael shares the South column with Amaymon. The III.24 order would pair him with Egin in the North.
goetic.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) II ch. 7 (Scale of Four); cf. III ch. 24; Eng. tr. 1651

goetic.name: Orience (Oriens)
goetic.role: king of the air, of the East
goetic.group: Variant kings — Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26)
goetic.extra: MS c.1577-83. MS p. 73: 'Orience R[ex] of the east'. MS p. 81 section: Oriens reigns in the east; his twelve chief spirits begin with Baall and Agaros. Messenger: Femell / Bellfarto.
goetic.note: The manuscript's Office of Spirits opens by naming four kings of the air, with Orience over the East. A later section repeats this and lists twelve principal spirits under him.
goetic.source: Folger Shakespeare Library MS V.b.26, 'Officium de spirittibus', MS pp. 73 and 81-82 (transcription by J. H. Peterson and D. Harms, esotericarchives.com/folger; printed as The Book of Oberon, 2015)

goetic.name: Paymon
goetic.role: king of the air, of the West
goetic.group: Variant kings — Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26)
goetic.extra: MS p. 73: 'Paymon R[ex] of the west'. Belferth is called messenger of the king of the west. Beliall heads his twelve (MS p. 83). Agrees with Agrippa.
goetic.note: Paymon holds the West in the Oberon set.
goetic.source: Folger MS V.b.26, MS pp. 73-74 and 82-83 (Peterson and Harms transcription)

goetic.name: Amaymon
goetic.role: king of the air, of the South
goetic.group: Variant kings — Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26)
goetic.extra: MS p. 73: 'Amaymon R[ex] of the southe'. MS p. 74: the master turns into the South to receive him. His twelve include Asmoday, Bileth and Astaroth (MS p. 82). Agrees with Agrippa.
goetic.note: Amaymon holds the South in the Oberon set. The operator is told to face south to receive him, and the text warns that he is very perilous.
goetic.source: Folger MS V.b.26, MS pp. 73-74 and 82 (Peterson and Harms transcription)

goetic.name: Egine (Egyn, Egin)
goetic.role: king of the air, of the North
goetic.group: Variant kings — Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26)
goetic.extra: MS p. 73: 'Egine R[ex] of the North'. MS p. 74: look to the North when calling him; 12,000 legions; messengers Rodabell and Lambricon. His twelve end with Annoboth (MS p. 84).
goetic.note: Egin holds the North in the Oberon set, and the operator must look north when calling him.
goetic.source: Folger MS V.b.26, MS pp. 73-75 and 83-84 (Peterson and Harms transcription)

goetic.name: Oriens
goetic.role: king of the air, of the East
goetic.group: Variant kings — Sloane MS 3853 (Offices of Spirits)
goetic.extra: Sloane 3853 fol. 258r. Add. 36674 fol. 65r names Scor, Algor and Sefon as under Oriens, king of the East.
goetic.note: This short English offices-of-spirits text names four kings of the air, with Oriens in the East.
goetic.source: British Library Sloane MS 3853 fol. 258r, in J. H. Peterson, 'The Offices of Spirits, excerpted from Sloane 3853, Wellcome 110, and Ad. 36674' (esotericarchives.com/solomon/offices.htm)

goetic.name: Paymon
goetic.role: king of the air, of the West
goetic.group: Variant kings — Sloane MS 3853 (Offices of Spirits)
goetic.extra: Sloane 3853 fol. 258r
goetic.note: Paymon is the king of the West in this list.
goetic.source: BL Sloane MS 3853 fol. 258r (Peterson, Offices of Spirits, esotericarchives.com)

goetic.name: Amaymon
goetic.role: king of the air, of the South
goetic.group: Variant kings — Sloane MS 3853 (Offices of Spirits)
goetic.extra: Sloane 3853 fol. 258r. Add. 36674 fol. 65r (as 'Amamion') puts Partas and Gamor under him as king of the South.
goetic.note: Amaymon is the king of the South in this list.
goetic.source: BL Sloane MS 3853 fol. 258r (Peterson, Offices of Spirits, esotericarchives.com)

goetic.name: Egim (Egin)
goetic.role: king of the air, of the North
goetic.group: Variant kings — Sloane MS 3853 (Offices of Spirits)
goetic.extra: Sloane 3853 fol. 258r spells 'Egim'. Add. 36674 fol. 65r puts Vmbra and Anaboth under Egin, king of the North.
goetic.note: Egim is the king of the North in this list.
goetic.source: BL Sloane MS 3853 fol. 258r (Peterson, Offices of Spirits, esotericarchives.com)

goetic.name: Oriens
goetic.group: Variant kings — Liber 777 (Crowley 1909)
goetic.extra: row 11 (Aleph / Air); col. LVII gives '(E) Mezrach' on the same row
goetic.note: In 777's Demon Kings column Oriens stands on the Air row, which the Four Quarters column makes East.
goetic.source: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909), col. LXVIII 'The Demon Kings' read against col. LVII 'The Four Quarters' (app 777.json)

goetic.name: Ariton
goetic.group: Variant kings — Liber 777 (Crowley 1909)
goetic.extra: row 23 (Mem / Water); col. LVII: '(W) Maareb'. Mathers' 1904 footnote equates Ariton with Egyn, who is North in Agrippa and Oberon.
goetic.note: Ariton stands on the Water row, which 777 makes West.
goetic.source: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909), cols. LXVIII and LVII (app 777.json)

goetic.name: Paimon
goetic.group: Variant kings — Liber 777 (Crowley 1909)
goetic.extra: row 31 (Shin / Fire); col. LVII: '(S) Darom'
goetic.note: Paimon stands on the Fire row, which 777 makes South. This differs from the Goetia's West.
goetic.source: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909), cols. LXVIII and LVII (app 777.json)

goetic.name: Amaimon
goetic.group: Variant kings — Liber 777 (Crowley 1909)
goetic.extra: row 32 bis (Earth); col. LVII: '(N) Tzaphon'
goetic.note: Amaimon stands on the Earth row, which 777 makes North. This differs from the Goetia's East.
goetic.source: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909), cols. LXVIII and LVII (app 777.json)

goetic.name: Oriens (Urieus)
goetic.role: king of the evil spirits of the East
goetic.group: Agrippa — kings of evil spirits of the four parts (cross-reference)
goetic.extra: II.7 table: 'Oriens' (row 'Four Princes of spirits, upon the four angles of the world'); III.18: 'Urieus, King of the East'
goetic.note: One of four powerful kings Agrippa sets over the evil spirits according to the four parts of the world.
goetic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 18; Bk II ch. 7

goetic.name: Paymon
goetic.role: king of the evil spirits of the West
goetic.group: Agrippa — kings of evil spirits of the four parts (cross-reference)
goetic.extra: cf. goetia.json #9 Paimon, whom the 1904 Goetia says is to be observed towards the West (agrees)
goetic.note: Agrippa's King of the West; this agrees with the Goetia's instruction to look West for Paimon.
goetic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 18; Bk II ch. 7

goetic.name: Egyn (Egin)
goetic.role: king of the evil spirits of the North
goetic.group: Agrippa — kings of evil spirits of the four parts (cross-reference)
goetic.extra: II.7: 'Egyn'; III.18: 'Egin, King of the North'
goetic.note: Agrippa's King of the North among the four kings of the evil spirits.
goetic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 18; Bk II ch. 7

goetic.name: Amaymon
goetic.role: king of the evil spirits of the South
goetic.group: Agrippa — kings of evil spirits of the four parts (cross-reference)
goetic.extra: CONFLICT: goetia.json #70 Seere (1904 Goetia) calls Amaymon 'King of the East'; Asmoday (#32) and Gaap (#33) are also tied to Amaymon
goetic.note: Agrippa's King of the South, while the Goetia puts Amaymon in the East.
goetic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 18; Bk II ch. 7

goetic.name: Samael
goetic.group: Agrippa — four princes of devils offensive in the elements (cross-reference)
goetic.extra: Heb. סמאל; III.18 spells it 'Samuel', listed first to match Urieus of the East; II.7 puts it in the Fire/East column; both readings agree on East
goetic.note: First of the four princes of devils in Agrippa's scale of four, in the Fire/East column; III.18 also pairs this name with the King of the East.
goetic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk II ch. 7; Bk III ch. 18

goetic.name: Azazel
goetic.group: Agrippa — four princes of devils offensive in the elements (cross-reference)
goetic.extra: Heb. עזאזל; CONFLICT: II.7 column gives Air/West, but III.18 lists the Hebrew names in the kings' order (East, South, West, North), which would put Azazel in the South
goetic.note: One of the four princes of devils in Agrippa's scale of four, in the Air/West column; Agrippa's own ch. 18 ordering implies the South instead.
goetic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk II ch. 7; Bk III ch. 18

goetic.name: Azael
goetic.group: Agrippa — four princes of devils offensive in the elements (cross-reference)
goetic.extra: Heb. עזאל; CONFLICT: II.7 column gives Water/North, but the III.18 ordering would put Azael in the West
goetic.note: One of the four princes of devils in Agrippa's scale of four, in the Water/North column; Agrippa's own ch. 18 ordering implies the West instead.
goetic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk II ch. 7; Bk III ch. 18

goetic.name: Mahazael
goetic.group: Agrippa — four princes of devils offensive in the elements (cross-reference)
goetic.extra: Heb. מהזאל; III.18 spells it 'Mahazuel'; CONFLICT: II.7 column gives Earth/South, but the III.18 ordering would put it in the North
goetic.note: One of the four princes of devils in Agrippa's scale of four, in the Earth/South column; Agrippa's own ch. 18 ordering implies the North instead.
goetic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk II ch. 7; Bk III ch. 18

goetic.name: Carnesiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Emperors
goetic.extra: Sl. 3825 variant: Carnesiell. 1000 great and 100 lesser dukes; 12 chief dukes named. Serves: day and night. Trithemius, Steganographia I.17.
goetic.note: Chief emperor ruling in the East. He may appear by day or night with an immense retinue, though far fewer come when only one of his dukes is called.
goetic.source: Lemegeton II, Theurgia-Goetia, BL Sloane MS 3825 fol. 118r (J. H. Peterson transcription, esotericarchives.com); cross-check Trithemius, Steganographia (1606) I.17

goetic.name: Caspiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Emperors
goetic.extra: 200 great and 400 lesser dukes; 12 chief dukes named. Day or night: not stated. Trithemius I.18.
goetic.note: Chief emperor ruling in the South. His dukes are described as stubborn and churlish.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 118v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.18

goetic.name: Amenadiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Emperors
goetic.extra: Trithemius: Armenadiel. 300 great and 500 lesser dukes; 12 named. Serves: any hour of day or night; his dukes take two hours each in turn.
goetic.note: Great emperor of the West. He may be called at any hour, while his twelve dukes are called in pairs of hours through the day and night.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 119r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.19

goetic.name: Demoriel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Emperors
goetic.extra: 400 great and 600 lesser dukes; 12 named, each with 1140 servants. Serves: day and night, his dukes by pairs of hours as for Amenadiel.
goetic.note: Great and mighty emperor of the North. His dukes are called by the same hour rule as Amenadiel's.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 119v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.20

goetic.name: Pamersiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: Trithemius wind: Oriens (I.1). 11 dukes named. Serves: DAY only. Nature: evil and false.
goetic.note: First and chief spirit of the East under Carnesiel. His spirits are called by day with great care; they are false, but good for driving spirits of darkness out of haunted places.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 120r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.1

goetic.name: Padiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: MS: 'East and by South'. Trithemius wind: Subsolanus (I.2); Trithemius' figure: Podiel. Azimuth uses the literal 32-point value; on Trithemius' evenly spaced 16-wind rose this slot would be 112.5° (ESE). 10,000 spirits by day and 20,000 by night. Nature: good.
goetic.note: Rules as king in the East by South, with ten thousand spirits by day and twenty thousand by night, all good and trustworthy.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 120v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.2

goetic.name: Camuel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: Trithemius wind: Eurus (I.3); Trithemius' figure: Cimuel. 10 day and 10 night servants named. Serves: day and night.
goetic.note: Rules the south-east part of the world. His servants appear beautiful and courteous; the text says those of the day appear by night and those of the night by day.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 121r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.3

goetic.name: Aseliel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: MS: 'South and by East'. Trithemius wind: Euroauster (I.4). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 157.5° (SSE). 10 chiefs by day and 20 by night; 8 + 8 named. The spelling 'Aschiel' does not occur in Sl. 3825 or Trithemius.
goetic.note: Governs as king under Carnesiel in the South by East. His spirits are courteous, loving and beautiful to see.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 121v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.4

goetic.name: Barmiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: Trithemius wind: Auster (I.5). 10 dukes by day and 20 by night; 8 + 8 named. Serves: day and night. Nature: good.
goetic.note: First and chief spirit under Caspiel, ruling as king of the South, with dukes for both day and night who obey willingly.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 122r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.5

goetic.name: Gediel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: MS: 'South & by West'. Trithemius wind: Austroafricus (I.6). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 202.5° (SSW). 20 by day and 20 by night; 8 + 8 named.
goetic.note: Rules as king in the South by West, with chief spirits for day and night who are loving and courteous.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 122v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.6

goetic.name: Asyriel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: Trithemius: Asiriel, wind Africus (I.7). 20 dukes by day and 20 by night; 8 + 8 named. Day dukes are called by day and night dukes by night.
goetic.note: A mighty king of the south-west part of the world. All his dukes are good-natured and willing.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 123r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.7

goetic.name: Maseriel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: MS: 'West, and by South'. Trithemius wind: Favonius (I.8). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 247.5° (WSW). 12 by day and 12 by night named, each with 30 servants.
goetic.note: Rules as king in the dominion of the West by South. His spirits are good by nature; those of the day are called by day and those of the night by night.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 123v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.8

goetic.name: Malgaras
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: Trithemius wind: Occidens (I.9). 30 dukes by day and 30 by night; 12 + 12 named. Serves: day and night.
goetic.note: First under the emperor of the West, ruling as king in the West. His courteous dukes appear two by two with their servants.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 124r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.9

goetic.name: Dorochiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: MS: 'West, and by North'. Trithemius: Dorothiel, wind Chorus (I.10). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 292.5° (WNW). 40 by day and 40 by night; 24 + 24 named, called by planetary hours.
goetic.note: A mighty prince ruling in the West by North. His good-natured dukes are called two per planetary hour through the day and night.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 124v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.10

goetic.name: Usiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: Trithemius: Vsiel, wind Subcircius (I.11). 40 diurnal and 40 nocturnal dukes; 14 + 14 named.
goetic.note: A mighty prince ruling as king in the north-west. His dukes are said to have more power than any others to hide or reveal treasure.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 125v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.11

goetic.name: Cabariel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: The Sl. 3825 heading gives no point. Sl. 2731 adds 'West & by North', which would duplicate Dorochiel. The conjuration says 'North & by West', and Trithemius' Circius (I.12) lies between Subcircius (NW) and Septentrio (N). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 337.5° (NNW). 50 by day (good) and 50 by night (evil).
goetic.note: His conjuration places him as king in the North by West. His day dukes are good and obedient; his night dukes are evil and deceitful.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 126v, conjuration (Peterson transcription, with Sl. 2731 variant); Trithemius, Steganographia I.12

goetic.name: Raysiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: Trithemius wind: Septentrio (I.13). 50 by day and 50 by night; 16 day (good) and 14 night (evil) named.
goetic.note: First under the emperor of the North, ruling as king in the North. His day dukes are good and his night dukes evil and stubborn.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 127r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.13

goetic.name: Symiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: MS: 'North & by Easte'. Trithemius wind: Aquilo (I.14). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 22.5° (NNE). 10 by day and 1000 by night; 10 + 10 named.
goetic.note: Rules as king in the North by East. His day dukes are good, while his night dukes are stubborn and unwilling.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 127v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.14

goetic.name: Armadiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: Trithemius wind: Boreas (I.15). 15 chief dukes with 1260 servants each. Serves: day and night, divided into 15 parts from sunrise.
goetic.note: Rules as king in the north-east part. His good dukes are called in turn through the day and night, which is divided into fifteen parts.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 128r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.15

goetic.name: Baruchas
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
goetic.extra: MS: 'East and by North'. Trithemius wind: Vulturnus (I.16). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 67.5° (ENE). 15 chief dukes, 7040 servants. Serves: day and night in 15 parts.
goetic.note: Rules as king in the East by North. His dukes are good and are called through the day and night in fifteen parts, as with Armadiel.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 128v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.16

goetic.name: Geradiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: Sl. 3825 also spells it Garadiel. No dukes; 18,150 servants. Serves: day and night, with the number of servants varying by planetary hour. Trithemius I.21.
goetic.note: First of the eleven princes who wander the air with no fixed place, so the facing direction does not matter. He is called alone, and more or fewer servants come depending on the hour.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 129r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.21

goetic.name: Buriel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: 12 dukes (one per night hour), 880 servants each. Serves: NIGHT only. Nature: evil. Trithemius I.22.
goetic.note: His spirits are evil, hated by all other spirits, and hate the day, so they are called only at night. They appear as serpents with a maiden's head.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 129v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.22

goetic.name: Hydriel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: 100 great and 200 lesser dukes; 12 named. Serves: day and night by planetary hours. Trithemius I.23.
goetic.note: His courteous dukes come by day or night as serpents with maidens' heads, and they delight in waters and moist ground.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 130r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.23

goetic.name: Pirichiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: Trithemius: Pyrichiel (I.24). Knights instead of dukes: 8 named, 2000 servants. Called according to planetary motion; day or night is not specified.
goetic.note: A wandering prince who has knights instead of dukes, all good by nature.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 130v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.24

goetic.name: Emoniel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: 100 princes and dukes plus 20 under-dukes; 12 named. Serves: day and night in planetary order. Trithemius I.25.
goetic.note: A good-natured wandering prince whose dukes come willingly by day or night and mostly dwell in woods.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 131r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.25

goetic.name: Icosiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: 100 dukes and 300 companions; 15 named, 2200 servants. Serves: day and night, the 24 hours divided into 15 parts from sunrise.
goetic.note: His good-natured dukes most often appear in houses.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 131v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.26

goetic.name: Soleviel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: Trithemius: Soleuiel (I.27). 200 dukes and 200 companions; 12 named, 1840 servants. Serves: day and night by planetary hours.
goetic.note: A wandering prince whose dukes and companions change places every year; all are good and obedient.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 132r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.27

goetic.name: Menadiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: Trithemius I.28 (printed 'Menachiel'). 20 dukes and 100 companions; 6 + 6 named, 390 servants. Called according to planetary motion, alternating a duke and a companion.
goetic.note: A good, obedient wandering prince. A duke and then a companion are called in successive planetary hours.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 132v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.28

goetic.name: Macariel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: 12 chief dukes named, 400 servants. Serves: day and night in planetary order.
goetic.note: A wandering prince whose dukes are good by nature and obedient to the exorcist.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 133r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.29

goetic.name: Uriel (Theurgia)
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: Not the archangel. 10 chief and 100 lesser dukes; 10 named, 650 servants. Day or night: not stated. Nature: evil.
goetic.note: A wandering prince whose dukes are evil, unwilling and false, and appear as serpents with maidens' heads.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 133v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.30

goetic.name: Bidiel
goetic.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
goetic.extra: Trithemius: Bydiel (I.31). 20 dukes and 200 lesser dukes; 10 named, 2400 servants. Day or night: not stated.
goetic.note: The last wandering prince. His good dukes change office and place every year and appear in beautiful human form.
goetic.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 134r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.31

goetic.name: Varcan
goetic.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
goetic.extra: Ministers: Tus, Andas, Cynabal. Latin wind: Boreas (also in Folger V.b.26: 'subditi Boreae'), which Turner renders 'North-winde'.
goetic.note: King of the aerial spirits of Sunday, under the North wind. His spirits bring gold, gems, riches, favour and honours.
goetic.source: Heptameron (attrib. Peter de Abano), Considerations of Sunday; Eng. R. Turner in The Fourth Book of Occult Philosophy (1655; B. Rowe transcription)

goetic.name: Arcan
goetic.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
goetic.extra: Ministers: Bilet, Missabu, Abuzaha. Latin wind: Zephyrus, 'the wind of the Moon'.
goetic.note: King of Monday's aerial spirits, under the West wind, which the text calls the wind of the Moon. They give silver, carry things from place to place and reveal secrets.
goetic.source: Heptameron (Turner 1655), Considerations of Monday

goetic.name: Samax
goetic.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
goetic.extra: Ministers: Carmax, Ismoli, Paffran. Latin wind: Subsolanus.
goetic.note: King of Tuesday's aerial spirits, under the East wind. They cause war, death and burnings, and can supply soldiers.
goetic.source: Heptameron (Turner 1655), Considerations of Tuesday

goetic.name: Mediat (Modiat)
goetic.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
goetic.extra: Turner: 'Mediat, or Modiat'. Ministers: Suquinos, Sallales. Wind: 'Southwest-winde' (Africus).
goetic.note: King of Wednesday's aerial spirits, under the south-west wind. They give metals, reveal things past and future, and teach lost sciences.
goetic.source: Heptameron (Turner 1655), Considerations of Wednesday

goetic.name: Suth
goetic.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
goetic.extra: Turner: 'Suth, Rex'. Ministers: Maguth, Gutrix. Wind: South (Auster).
goetic.note: King of Thursday's aerial spirits, under the South wind. They bring love, mirth and peace, and cause or cure illness.
goetic.source: Heptameron (Turner 1655), Considerations of Thursday

goetic.name: Sarabotes (Sarabotres)
goetic.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
goetic.extra: Ministers: Amabiel, Aba, Abalidoth, Flaef. Wind: West (Zephyrus).
goetic.note: King of Friday's aerial spirits, under the West wind. They give silver, stir desire, reconcile enemies and make marriages.
goetic.source: Heptameron (Turner 1655), Considerations of Friday

goetic.name: Maymon
goetic.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
goetic.extra: Ministers: Abumalith, Assaibi, Balidet. Wind: 'Southwest-winde' (Africus). Peterson notes a manuscript variant 'Amaymon'.
goetic.note: King of Saturday's aerial spirits, under the south-west wind. They sow discord and hatred and can kill or maim. The name is a clear cognate of Amaymon.
goetic.source: Heptameron (Turner 1655), Considerations of Saturday

angelic.name: Varcan
angelic.role: King of the Angels of the Air
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — Angels of the Air (wind: North)
angelic.extra: Turner: 'Varcan, King'; Latin 'Varcan rex' and wind name Boreas per T.S. 2002; Sun, fourth heaven; angels of the day Michael, Dardiel, Huratapal
angelic.note: King of the aerial angels ruling Sunday, placed under the North wind; the text says Sunday's aerial spirits bring gold, gems, riches, favour and honours and remove or cause sickness.
angelic.source: Heptameron (attrib. Peter de Abano), tr. Robert Turner in Agrippa's Fourth Book of Occult Philosophy (London 1655), 'Considerations of the Lords day' (B. Rowe e-text 2000; checked against the 1655 page scans on Wikisource)

angelic.name: Tus
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — Angels of the Air (wind: North)
angelic.extra: variant Tys (T.S. 2002, from the Latin)
angelic.note: One of Varcan's three ministers among Sunday's aerial angels, under the North wind.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Andas
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — Angels of the Air (wind: North)
angelic.note: One of Varcan's three ministers among Sunday's aerial angels, under the North wind.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Cynabal
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — Angels of the Air (wind: North)
angelic.note: One of Varcan's three ministers among Sunday's aerial angels, under the North wind.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Samael
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the East
angelic.extra: 4th heaven (Machen per T.S. 2002)
angelic.note: One of the fourth-heaven angels to be called toward the East on Sunday.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Baciel
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the East
angelic.note: One of the fourth-heaven angels to be called toward the East on Sunday.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Atel
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the East
angelic.note: One of the fourth-heaven angels to be called toward the East on Sunday.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Gabriel
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the East
angelic.extra: Turner prints Gabriel; T.S. 2002 (following the Latin of Agrippa's Opera, c.1600) reads Fabriel
angelic.note: Listed among the fourth-heaven angels to be called toward the East on Sunday; the Latin reading Fabriel suggests Turner may have normalised the name.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'; variant from Frater T.S. rev. ed. (Celephais Press, 2002)

angelic.name: Vionairaba
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the East
angelic.extra: variant Vionatraba (T.S. 2002)
angelic.note: One of the fourth-heaven angels to be called toward the East on Sunday.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Anael
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the West
angelic.note: One of the fourth-heaven angels to be called toward the West on Sunday.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Pabel
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the West
angelic.note: One of the fourth-heaven angels to be called toward the West on Sunday.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Ustael
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the West
angelic.note: One of the fourth-heaven angels to be called toward the West on Sunday.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Burchat
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the West
angelic.note: One of the fourth-heaven angels to be called toward the West on Sunday.
angelic.source: Heptameron, tr. Turner 1655, 'Considerations of the Lords day'

angelic.name: Suceratos
angelic.group: Heptameron — Sunday — angels of the West

angelic.name: Michael
angelic.role: prince of the angels, over the East wind
angelic.group: Agrippa — four princes of angels over the winds
angelic.extra: Heb. מיכאל; II.7 Scale of Four column: Fire, heat, summer, East
angelic.note: Agrippa sets Michael over the eastern wind and the eastern part of the world; his scale of four also puts him in the Fire/East column.
angelic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (tr. J.F., London 1651), Bk III ch. 24; Bk II ch. 7 (Scale of the number four, row 'Four Angels ruling over the corners of the world')

angelic.name: Raphael
angelic.role: prince of the angels, over the West wind
angelic.group: Agrippa — four princes of angels over the winds
angelic.extra: Heb. רפאל; II.7 column: Air, moisture, spring, West
angelic.note: Agrippa sets Raphael over the western wind, the opposite of the Golden Dawn's Raphael in the East.
angelic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 24; Bk II ch. 7

angelic.name: Gabriel
angelic.role: prince of the angels, over the North wind
angelic.group: Agrippa — four princes of angels over the winds
angelic.extra: Heb. גבריאל; II.7 column: Water, cold, winter, North
angelic.note: Agrippa sets Gabriel over the northern wind (the Golden Dawn puts him in the West).
angelic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 24; Bk II ch. 7

angelic.name: Nariel (Uriel)
angelic.role: prince of the angels, over the South wind
angelic.group: Agrippa — four princes of angels over the winds
angelic.extra: III.24 names him Nariel, adding that some call him Uriel; the II.7 table prints Uriel; II.7 column: Earth, dryness, autumn, South
angelic.note: Agrippa sets Nariel, also called Uriel, over the southern wind (the Golden Dawn puts Auriel in the North).
angelic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 24; Bk II ch. 7

angelic.name: Seraph
angelic.group: Agrippa — rulers of the elements (Scale of Four)

angelic.note: Agrippa's ruler of Fire, which falls in the East column of his scale of four.
angelic.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk II ch. 7 (table row 'Four rulers of the Elements'); Bk III ch. 24

angelic.name: Cherub

angelic.name: Tharsis
angelic.group: Agrippa — rulers of the elements (Scale of Four)

angelic.note: Agrippa's ruler of Water, which falls in the North column of his scale of four.

angelic.name: Ariel
angelic.group: Agrippa — rulers of the elements (Scale of Four)

angelic.name: Gabriel
angelic.group: Midrash — four angels around the Throne (Bamidbar Rabbah 2:10)
angelic.extra: 'before Him', matched with the kingdom of Judah and with Moses and Aaron, whom the text places in the east
angelic.note: The midrash places Gabriel in front of the divine Throne, matching Judah's camp in the east.
angelic.source: Bamidbar (Numbers) Rabbah 2:10 (Hebrew text on Sefaria; English: Sefaria Midrash Rabbah 2022, CC-BY); camp layout per Numbers 2

angelic.name: Michael
angelic.role: archangel at the right of the Throne
angelic.group: Midrash — four angels around the Throne (Bamidbar Rabbah 2:10)
angelic.extra: 'at His right', matched with Reuben, whose camp lay south (Num. 2:10); the compass point comes from Numbers, not stated in the midrash itself
angelic.note: The midrash places Michael at the Throne's right, matching Reuben's camp on the south.

angelic.name: Raphael
angelic.role: archangel of the fourth side of the Throne
angelic.group: Midrash — four angels around the Throne (Bamidbar Rabbah 2:10)
angelic.extra: matched with Ephraim, whose camp lay west (Num. 2:18); the midrash links his name to healing the breach of Jeroboam, who came from Ephraim
angelic.note: The midrash pairs Raphael with Ephraim's camp on the west side.

angelic.name: Uriel
angelic.role: archangel at the left of the Throne
angelic.group: Midrash — four angels around the Throne (Bamidbar Rabbah 2:10)
angelic.extra: 'at His left', matched with Dan, which the text says is in the north
angelic.note: The midrash places Uriel at the Throne's left, matching Dan's camp in the north.

angelic.note: King of the Water tablet, which the Golden Dawn puts in the West.
angelic.source: Liber Chanokh (Equinox I:7–8, 1912), explanation of the tablets, Plate V 'The Great Watch-Tower of the West, attributed to Water' and invocation; Dee readings per enochian.blog and Augoeides blog (Stenwick)

angelic.name: Iczhhcal
